title: Prompt shadow indexing and GPU-resident slab cursors for cross-request reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Redundant prompt prefix material across concurrent requests causes GPU memory churn and repeated KV-loads. Existing per-request KV materialization and full-fragment dedupe are effective but leave a gap for mid-frequency short prefixes and session-level reuse patterns.

Proposal summary: Introduce a lightweight shadow index that maps canonicalized prompt headers (normalized token sequences + template slots) to compact descriptor entries. Maintain small GPU-resident slab cursors that point into a shared KV slab store; cursors are reference-counted and pinned opportunistically for hot descriptors to avoid re-copying K/V into per-request buffers. Integrate with the continuous batching pipeline so the scheduler can: 1) coalesce requests that share a descriptor, 2) prefetch pinned cursors into active batches, and 3) lazily materialize slots for low-frequency descriptors.

Goals: reduce per-request memory copies, increase cross-request KV hit-rate for short/mid-length prefixes, and keep GPU resident footprint predictable with controlled pinning eviction.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype integrates shadow index with scheduler and can be toggled via runtime flag
Observed 15-25% reduction in token-level GPU memory copies on mixed-traffic benchmarks vs baseline
Cross-request descriptor hit-rate >= 30% on our session-heavy replay workload (internal benchmark)
Pinning policy does not increase peak GPU memory beyond 6% of baseline in worst-case synthetic workload
Comprehensive metrics and dashboards added: descriptor_hits, descriptor_misses, pinned_cursor_count, avg_cursor_age
implementation_notes: Canonicalization: normalize whitespace, template slot ids, and apply lossy short-hash for descriptor key (64-bit) to keep index compact
Shadow index metadata kept in host memory; small hot-set replicated to GPU as a condensed table for fast lookup during batching
GPU-resident slab cursors store (cursor_id -> slab_offset,len,refcount,last_access_ts); cursors are lightweight (24 bytes)
Eviction: hybrid LRU + frequency aging; background sweeper demotes pins after X ms of inactivity; immediate unpin on memory pressure event
Integration points: continuous-batcher (scheduling hook), kv-store loader (materialization path), trace/span tagging for observability
Fallbacks: if descriptor canonicalization fails or key collision suspected, fall back to conservative full materialization for that request
Safety: pinning respects tenant isolation—only cursors for same tenant/model variant can be reused; cross-tenant reuse disabled
tests: Unit: canonicalizer edge cases, hash collision stress tests
Unit: cursor refcount and eviction invariants under concurrent pin/unpin
Integration: replay benchmark with session-heavy traces comparing baseline vs shadow-index enabled
Load: synthetic high-cardinality prefixes to validate memory caps and autoscaling response
Chaos: simulate OOM and verify sweeper and unpin logic recovers without request failures
rollout_plan: 1. Feature flag guarded behind runtime flag and tenant whitelist
2. Canary on low-traffic region for 24h with detailed metrics collection
3. Expand to 10% traffic split with safety monitor for pinned_cursor_count and memory rise
4. Full rollout if no regressions and performance targets met
5. Post-rollout: watchlist for odd descriptor collision patterns for 2 weeks
perf_targets: Descriptor lookup latency added to scheduling hot path < 25 microseconds (median)
End-to-end request latency regression <= 3% p95 when feature enabled for cold workloads
Target memory overhead of shadow-index metadata < 1% of host RAM and < 3% of GPU memory for hot-set
